requirement: Implement ResilientWorkerPool with start, submit, collect_results, and graceful shutdown using poison pill sentinels, process reaping on timeout, and clean queue feeder thread management.
skeleton: ResilientWorkerPool managing multiprocessing.Process workers and Queues.
caption: A multiprocessing worker pool with an explicit lifecycle and no third-party imports. The module-level _worker_entry loop polls its task queue with a 0.1 second timeout, ignoring queue.Empty and TimeoutError so a quiet queue is not an error, exits when it receives the STOP_SENTINEL string, doubles numeric or string items, and puts a success or error dict on the result queue. ResilientWorkerPool stores num_workers, defaulting to 2, an empty worker list, two queues that start as None, and a running flag. start returns immediately when already running, so a second call cannot orphan the first set of workers; otherwise it creates fresh task and result queues, starts num_workers processes on _worker_entry, and sets the flag. submit raises RuntimeError when the pool is not running or has no task queue, and otherwise enqueues the item. collect_results also raises RuntimeError on a stopped pool; it computes one deadline from time.monotonic plus the timeout, defaulting to one second, and for each expected item waits on the result queue for the remaining time with a floor of ten milliseconds, converting queue.Empty or a timeout into a TimeoutError with a message, so a missing result surfaces as an error instead of a hang. shutdown does nothing when not running; otherwise it enqueues one STOP_SENTINEL per worker so in-flight work finishes, joins each worker with a per-worker share of the timeout, terminates and joins again any worker still alive so no zombie remains, closes both queues and joins their feeder threads, and clears the running flag.

plan.intent: Manage a process pool with explicit start, submit, collect, and shutdown
constraints: Starting an already running pool is a no-op
Submitting to or collecting from a stopped pool raises RuntimeError
Collection shares one deadline across all results and raises TimeoutError when a result is missing
Shutdown sends one stop sentinel per worker, joins them, and terminates any survivor
Both queues are closed and the running flag cleared after shutdown

rationale.teaches: A worker pool with explicit lifecycle: submit refuses when not running, collect_results honors a deadline, shutdown sends a sentinel per worker, joins with a timeout, and terminates only the stragglers.
rationale.why: Pool lifecycle bugs hang or leak processes rather than raising. The fixture times every phase and checks that the worker processes are gone afterward.

ops.docstring: Run a pool of worker processes that survives a slow or stuck shutdown.

candidates.why_wrong: Terminated workers are never joined, so zombie processes remain after shutdown.
collect_results waits with no timeout, so a missing result blocks the caller forever.
submit on a stopped pool silently enqueues instead of raising RuntimeError.
start on a running pool rebuilds the worker list, so the original workers are orphaned and never shut down.
shutdown terminates every worker immediately without a sentinel, so in-flight tasks are killed instead of finished.
